title: Fake US thinktank set up and funded by Israel sought to game AI for propaganda

reading.body:
A fake think tank with no legal entity or named staff published over 560,000 words in 124 reports across nine days, designed to make AI chatbots cite its material as authoritative research. The Hanover Institute presented arguments on contested topics like Palestinian torture and Israeli military conduct as neutral scholarship, built on a platform optimized specifically to attract citations by systems like ChatGPT. The operation succeeded in placing content where AI systems retrieve it, but only one outlet reported on the campaign, so the scope of actual adoption by deployed chatbots is not established.

The failure occurred at the point where AI systems cite sources without verifying their legitimacy or independence. An AI system trained to find and quote authoritative research cannot distinguish between a real institution and a fabricated one if the fabrication is technically competent and accessible in its training data or retrieval systems. Catching this would have required either AI systems to verify the legal status and independence of sources before citing them, or the platforms hosting the think tank's work to vet their authors before accepting content designed for algorithmic amplification.

Whether the operation actually influenced chatbot outputs or shaped public opinion remains unclear from the reporting. The Israeli government's own officials reportedly questioned whether such efforts were effective.

reports.title: Fake US thinktank set up and funded by Israel sought to game AI for propaganda

summary:
# Summary

An Israeli-funded fake American think tank called the Hanover Institute published over 560,000 words across 124 reports in just nine days, designed to influence artificial intelligence chatbots to generate pro-Israel arguments. The institute, which does not exist as a legal entity and has no named staff, presented material on topics including Palestinian torture, Israeli war crimes, and Gaza starvation as neutral research. The operation was filed with the U.S. Justice Department as a foreign agent and was built on a commercial platform specifically designed to optimize content so that AI systems like ChatGPT would cite it.

The broader campaign, financed by tens of millions of dollars from the Israeli government and routed through the European advertising firm Havas Media, also includes other operations attempting to shape chatbot responses. Israeli officials have expressed skepticism about these public diplomacy efforts, with some calling them expensive failures. Meanwhile, American public opinion has shifted significantly against Israel, with recent polling showing declining support and growing belief that Israeli military actions constitute genocide, particularly among younger Americans and Democrats.
